scope: the entity id is NOT a plain 12-bit field at bit 1309: the body already had bits 000100000000 there yet the client decoded 4048

the_measurement.body_bits_1309_1320: 000100000000 (= 8 if read as a plain LSB-first 12-bit field)
the_measurement.conclusion: the id is not read as a straight 12-bit field from 1309

why: the read goes through 0x66EC30, which reads WHOLE BYTES starting at byte ([+0x20] >> 3) and then shifts within the byte using the bit offset
so the value depends on the byte alignment and on how the function combines the bytes, not on a clean bit slice
the earlier observation that one 12-bit read advances the position by 20 bits is the same phenomenon seen from the other side
what_this_invalidates: the plan to choose the entity id by writing bits 1309..1320
and my prediction that id 4048 is out of range for the map - that may still be true, but the id cannot be changed the way I assumed
what_is_needed: read the body of 0x66EC30 (0x66EC8D onwards) to learn exactly how it assembles N bits from bytes, including the shift direction and the byte order
then the id can be set deliberately and the 'small id' experiment becomes possible
the_other_observation: the client process was gone at the end of this run, so this body (changed bit 1, count 1, id whatever) makes it exit
whereas snapshot-id8.bin is byte-identical in the id bits to ent2, so the exit is the same behaviour ent2 already showed
